# Changelog

## 2026-11-27: Endfield profile with the fused lite tier; the libHGP loop is not on the critical path (correction)

- `perf record -F 999` (20 s, with 0089 + 0090, deb preload without the paths.c fix), samples by thread: the thread that runs the `libHGP.so` loop (tid named "UnityMain", a second thread with the creator's name) is 27.6% of all samples, 99% in translated code, 82% in the two loop regions: a background scan thread that spins one core. It is NOT the thread that loads the game: the earlier reading ("UnityMain spends 82% of its time in this loop") confused the two threads of that name. That is why fusing its cmp + b.cond gained only ~3% of load time.
- The real main thread (UnityMain 648894, 27.9% of samples): 58% translated code (flat: the top region is 10.7%, then il2cpp regions at 2-3%), ~20% kernel (syscalls, page faults), ~10% libberberis (AddAndLockForTranslation, MachineCode::PerformRelocations/Grow, ExitRegion: translating regions), ~6% libc. "Sync Present Thread" (25%) runs libunity regions, also off the load's critical path. Next levers by this split: general lite code quality (flat, so only broad changes pay: fewer memory round trips of ARM registers across region exits, TBI mask, chaining), the ~10% translation cost (a persisted translation cache), the kernel 20% (needs kernel symbols: perf needs root for kptr_restrict; the paths.c fix is not in the deb yet, so these runs still had the realpath chains).

## 2026-11-27: neural upscaler experiment (tools/nnup)
- AIDA64 freeze at neural 40 (owner, 2026-11-27; relaunch in the default instance with the deb b2e7bf20): the shell log ends with "all 8 output buffers are held by the compositor" while AIDA64 draws at the display's rate (its Display screen reports 180 Hz) and the window was 1376x553 -> a landscape window: each neural frame is 3-11 ms on the shell's single main thread, so a window that draws flat out keeps the whole shell (every window's frames and input) busy. `sharpen.c`: besides the 25 ms-per-frame rule, a duty-cycle guard: over 60 % of a second spent in neural frames ends the pass for that window (log "kept the shell busy N% of the last second"), FSR 1 runs from then on. Not run in the live shell (needs a deb); tested only that nothing else changed (tests/vm/sharpen.py neural check). Real fix still open: run the pass without blocking the shell's main thread (a fence polled later, or its own thread and GL context) and frame-rate-limit it.
- Smaller student shipped (2026-11-27): `bridge/native/nn/student.bin` is now the 32688 MAC/px student (channels 16,24,32,32,32; `distill.py s2.pt 12000 16,24,32,32,32`, 12000 steps) instead of the 92808 one: PSNR on the held-out crops (0.6 / 0.5 / 0.4) 39.73 / 39.83 / 34.10 against the larger one's 39.73 / 39.88 / 34.12 (a 20000-step run of the larger net: 39.78 / 39.83 / 34.27; a 14292 MAC/px net: 39.42 / 39.26 / 33.73, not shipped); GL vs torch 57.8 dB. tests/vm/sharpen.py neural check passes at 75/60/50/40.
- Render scale 40 in the manager: the slider's minimum follows the filter (`Backend.render-scale-min`: 40 with Neural, 65 with FSR 1; changing the filter updates it), the settings help text says 40..200 (below 65 only with the neural filter). The manager builds (ninja -C manager/b).
- Fix after the owner's report (AIDA64: UI not drawn, freezing, 2026-11-27, with the neural filter at render scale 40): (1) the render scale minimum was still 65 in `bridge/hals/graphics/display.c` and `AppHost.readRenderScale`, so scale 40 ran at 65 (now 40 there; cli/run.cpp keeps FSR 1 at 65); (2) the shell's main thread waits for each frame, so a slow neural pass (a big window, a GPU busy with a game) stalls every window: `sharpen.c` now measures each neural frame and, when the moving average is over 25 ms for 12 frames, runs FSR 1 for that window (log: "the neural pass takes N ms per frame"); with APKLAYER_RUNTIME_DEBUG it logs the network start-up and the first frames' times. Not reproduced: in an own instance AIDA64 at 65 % draws and the pass takes 7.6 ms per frame (429x764 -> 660x1176, incl. the GPU wait); the cause of the owner's freeze is not confirmed (large window, other apps on the GPU, or something else: needs the shell.log of that run).
- Wired into the settings (after the student below): `render-filter neural` (cli/manage.cpp accepts it, run.cpp passes `APKLAYER_RENDER_FILTER=neural`, bridge/hals/graphics/display.c sets DMABUF_FRAME flags bit 18, client.c -> `window.neural` -> `sharpen_set_neural`), the network loads at the first frame that wants it from `$APKLAYER_NN_WEIGHTS`, the installed `share/apklayer/bridge/native/nn/student.bin` or the build tree's copy; FSR 1 runs where it cannot (log: "neural upscaler unavailable"). Render scale 40..64 is accepted and kept only with the neural filter (run.cpp: otherwise 65). Manager: "Neural (beta)" button, the slider from 40. Test: tests/vm/sharpen.py (neural at 75/60/50/40 against FSR 1 on its synthetic text picture: +0.40, -0.09, +0.20, +0.53 dB, sharper by x1.06-1.26; all pass). Not run: the shell in a real window with a game (the sharpen-test program only).
- Student (tools/nnup/distill.py, export_student.py): five valid 3x3 convs 3-24-32-48-64-64 + a sixth to 12 channels + pixel shuffle + bilinear 2x, 92808 MAC/px (waifu2x: 551k), trained 6000 steps on 17 local images against the teacher's output at render scales 0.4-0.8. PSNR on the held-out crops (0.6 / 0.5 / 0.4): 39.73 / 39.88 / 34.12 against waifu2x 39.47 / 38.86 / 34.38 and FSR 1 37.38 / 37.27 / 32.83 (the FSR 1 numbers of the entries above came from a stale test binary: rebuilding it picked up the current FSR code; the gains of waifu2x there were about 0.8 dB too big). The GLES pass equals the torch student to 58 dB (a LeakyReLU on the last layer had given 45). Compute per 1080p frame on the RTX 5060 Ti: about 5 / 9 / 17 / 24 ms at render scale 0.4 / 0.5 / 0.6 / 0.75.
- Port (bridge/shell/sharpen_nn.c/.h, hooked in sharpen.c behind `APKLAYER_SHARPEN_NN=1` and `APKLAYER_NN_WEIGHTS=<file from tools/nnup/export_waifu.py>`; GLES 3.1 compute, FSR 1 runs where it cannot): waifu2x upconv_7 photo, six 3x3 layers + the 4x4 transposed conv as compute, 2x picture resampled by Catmull-Rom into the output dmabuf. `tools/nnup/check_gl.py`: the pass equals the PyTorch reference to 53 dB (42.19 dB against the original at 0.6; torch 42.77). No CMAA2, RCAS or temporal pass on this path. Not wired into settings yet; the render-scale minimum for it is meant to be 40 (change to 50 later if 40 looks bad).
- Speed (`tools/nnup/time_gl.py`, RTX 5060 Ti, 1080p output, ms per frame; includes the test program's readback, about 13 ms): naive version 334 / 214 / 152 at render scale 0.75 / 0.6 / 0.5; with shared-memory tiling and 2x2 pixels x 4 output layers per thread 182 / 123 / 88 (0.4: 60); FSR 1 in the same harness 16 / 13. The network is about 285 GMAC per frame at 0.5, so the tiled kernel runs at roughly a third of the card's fp32 peak: more speed needs fewer multiply-adds (a distilled smaller student), fp16, or tensor cores (Vulkan cooperative matrix).
- Question: a better upscaler than FSR 1. `tools/nnup/eval.py MODEL.pt <sharpen-test>`: three held-out 3440x1440 screenshots (not in the owner's repo, `~/Pictures/Schermafdrukken`), six 1280x720 crops, BOX-downscaled to render scale 0.75 and 0.6, upscaled back by the real FSR 1 pass (sharpen-test, GLES, `SHARPEN_MODIFIER=0x300000000606010` on NVIDIA; the pass needs the modifier) and by nets; PSNR/SSIM against the original. The luminance nets take Y, the colour differences go bicubic.
- Result (PSNR dB; 0.75 / 0.60): bilinear 38.00 / 35.75; FSR 1 38.31 / 36.59; own 15k-param net 38.56 / 36.24 (short training); own 60k-param net 38.15 / 35.81; pretrained ESPCN_x2 40.11 / 38.34; FSRCNN-small_x2 40.24 / 38.37; **FSRCNN_x2 40.54 / 38.82** (SSIM 0.9916 / 0.9863 against FSR 1's 0.9866 / 0.9792). FSRCNN_x2 is about 8k multiply-adds per source pixel (Y only), so it is cheap.
- waifu2x upconv_7 (nagadomi/waifu2x, MIT; RGB, 2x, ~0.55M multiply-adds per source pixel; `pretrained.Waifu`, weights fetched into ~/apklayer-nnup-work/w, 10 MB each as json): **photo 40.95 / 39.47** (SSIM 0.9926 / 0.9888), art 40.68 / 39.29: better than FSRCNN_x2 by 0.4-0.65 dB and than FSR 1 by 2.6-2.9 dB. Ignoring cost, waifu2x (photo) is the best of the pretrained models. Real-ESRGAN compact was not tried (1.2M multiply-adds per pixel).
- Caveats: the inputs are downscaled screenshots, not frames a game rendered natively (aliased); text and the game content need the same test on real frames. Not ported to a shader yet (`sharpen.c`, `sharpen_vk*.c`).
- Left on this PC for the port work: `~/apklayer-nnup-work` (torch + tensorflow venvs, 5.4 GB + TF; weights; own nets m1/m2): delete at the end of the task.

## 2026-11-27: game loading: berberis host-call overhead (binary_translation 0087, build running, not yet measured)

- Build log: `m libberberis_arm64` in ~/los24 (gsi_x86_64) on the Mac, started 16:2x.
- Profile of Endfield's cold load (own instance `endfield-load`, 30 GB data copy, `berberis.profiling`, `perf record -g`, 60 s): 54% translated code, 19% libberberis_arm64, 7.4% glibc, 3.8% proxy libc. Top symbols: `GuestThread::GlibcHostRecords()` 5.5%, `pthread_getspecific` 5.0%, `__errno_location` + `bionic___errno` + their PLT stubs ~3.5%: the errno swap every wrapped host call does (0003), also for `pthread_*` (return their code, never set errno) and `__errno`.
- Build done (`libberberis_arm64` 58cec244, gsi_x86_64). Measured on PGR (own instance `pgrload`, data copied, stopped at the update dialog/login, no taps): both libraries show the Kuro logo at 13-17 s and the update dialog at 29-31 s, so 0087 shows no difference at 4 s screenshot resolution; the dialog then waits on the network for 3 s (new) or ~85 s (stock), which is not load time. Endfield's fresh instance had a terms dialog in one run only. Needs a finer metric (in-process mark times, or CPU time to a fixed milestone) before judging 0087; instances deleted.
- In-process marks (PGR, fresh instance without game data, `APKLAYER_LOGCAT=1`, log lines stamped by a reader, 3 runs each, alternating): `loadLibrary lib_burst_0_0` (Unity's native load starts) to `CrashSightReport setGpuInfo` (engine has its GL context) = 8.72 / 8.74 / 8.77 s stock, 8.67 / 8.71 / 8.64 s with 0087 (-0.8%). Spread 0.1 s, so 0087 is a real but tiny gain in this phase; the pthread_getspecific/errno cost in Endfield's profile is not what dominates PGR's engine start. Instance deleted.
- `perf record` of the span (PGR, 8.7 s, 997 Hz): only 3.4 CPU-seconds over 8.7 s wall; UnityMain is in futex_do_wait in 115 of 118 samples, the Java looper is idle, thread-state sampling saw 5 runnable threads in total: the span is a WAIT, not translation or CPU. The CPU that is there: 38% kernel, `realpath`/`readlink` 18% (from the path layer: `other_scoped_resolved` ran for every path call because any symlink() at start-up sets `symlinks_made`), 5% berberis. Fixed in `paths.c` (see docs/PATCHES.md); the span stays 8.74-8.81 s (3 runs), i.e. it saves CPU on background threads but not wall time. `meson test path-layer` passes with and without the change. Not run: the VM groups (no tests/vm/local.conf on this PC). What UnityMain waits for is open: ptrace attach is blocked (ptrace_scope=1) and tracepoints are not available; needs `! sudo sysctl kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0` (then `strace -f -T -p` of the app JVM, or gdb on UnityMain) or running the app JVM under strace from its start.
- strace -f (ptrace_scope 0) of the span, thread names from /proc/<pid>/task: UnityMain, UnityChoreographer, UnityGfxDeviceWorker, the Android main thread each issue 1-1.5k futex/ioctl/read calls per second from t+3 s to the end: Unity is running its frame loop (splash and logo screens: Kuro logo, epilepsy notice, update check) and waits for vsync between frames; no thread blocks on a long call after t+1.6 s. So `setGpuInfo` fires at a fixed point of that splash sequence (8.7 s +/- 0.1 over 12 runs): the span measures the splash timer, not load work, and no CPU optimisation can move it. The earlier "UnityMain in futex 97%" was this vsync waiting. Also seen: each Background Job worker issues ~50 readlink per openat (the path layer's realpath chains, fixed in paths.c).
- **Endfield asset-load phase, measured (own instance `efm`, 30 GB data copy, no taps):** marks = a watcher (inotify IN_OPEN on the game's Android/data folder, stamps by a reader) timestamps the first open of `il2cpp/unity.ver`, `index_initial.json` (first .blc: asset index read), `ClientData/Local/Default.json`, the first mscorlib resource. 3 alternating cold runs each, stock vs 0087 + paths.c fix (libberberis 58cec244 and the new preload): unity.ver 6.21 -> 5.92 s, mscorlib resource 10.98 -> 10.57 s, index_initial 15.30 -> 14.82 s, Default.json 19.84 -> 19.24 s (about -3%, each of the 3 runs, spread 0.1 s; one stock run was an outlier at 27.9 s for index_initial, left out); process CPU at 42 s: 10.7-10.9k ticks -> 10.1-10.5k (-4%). So the two CPU fixes are worth ~0.5 s of the ~20 s to the game's data read, as the profile's ~15% for the wrapper overhead did not materialise in the wall time (guest code is 54-70%). Instance and copies deleted.
- Build log (2026-11-27): `m libberberis_arm64` (gsi_x86_64, Mac VM) with binary_translation 0088 (berberis.gear_threshold: the lite->heavy hotness threshold as a property/env, default 1000).
- **Lite tier, Endfield (own instance `efl`, 30 GB data copy; profile, then marks):** (1) `perf record -F 999` (20 s, perf map of berberis regions mapped by address): all 192k regions are `lite` (instance default `berberis.mode = lite-translate-or-interpret`, commit 5892bd50e); 1208 regions get samples, the top 10 take 47%, the top 100 56%. Two regions of `libHGP.so` (guest 0x...fd64 462 B and 0x...fd8c 157 B) take 30.5% of ALL samples, all on thread UnityMain (37% of the samples, so 82% of that thread's time in this window): a 9-instruction ARM64 loop stepping through 16-byte entries (`ldr x8,[x19,#24]; add x8,x8,x23; ldrb w9,[x8,#8]; tbz w9,#6; ...; add x23,x23,#16; cmp x22,x23; b.hi`), split into two regions by a `bl` on its rare path. Host code of the hot region (dumped from /proc/pid/mem): about 45 x86 instructions per iteration: every ARM memory access is `mov; shl 8; shr 8` (top-byte-ignore mask), `cmp` becomes `sub; lahf; seto; and; xor; mov [rbp+0xf8],ax` and `b.cond` reads it back with `bt WORD PTR [rbp+0xf8],n` (a store-forwarded memory test), and each region exit is `movabs rax,pc; cmp [rbp+0x360],2; je; movabs rcx,slot; mov ecx,[rcx]; jmp rcx`. (2) Two-gear is slower on Endfield, not faster: index_initial mark 18.0 s vs 15.8-16.9 s lite; with `berberis.gear_threshold` (new, 0088) at 20000 / 200000 / 2000000 it is 17.7 / 17.7 / 17.3-18.3 s: the threshold does not matter, even at 2M where no heavy compile can happen it is 9% slower than lite, so the cost is the self-profiling counters lite code carries in two-gear, and heavy-optimising hot regions buys nothing before the title screen. (3) Candidates, in order: fuse `cmp/subs/adds/tst` + `b.cond` (branch on the x86 flags before they are clobbered, store NZCV on both paths); one-instruction TBI mask (BMI2 `bzhi`, or skip the mask when the tag byte is known zero); chain regions directly instead of `mov ecx,[rcx]; jmp rcx`. Each touches the 80k-line lite translator and needs its exec/differential tests (lite_translate_region_exec_tests, differential_fuzz_tests, which run only in the Mac tree's host build); not started.
- **Correction (2026-11-27, found while committing the prebuilt):** the library I measured as "0087" in the PGR (-0.8%) and Endfield (-3%) comparisons was byte-identical (sha 58cec244) to the already committed 0086 prebuilt: the Mac build I used had started before the 0087 edit, so it did not contain it. Those two comparisons therefore compared the same libberberis. The PGR -0.8% is noise; the Endfield -3% came from the paths.c preload change alone (the preload copy was the only difference), 0087 is unmeasured by them. The first binary that contains 0087 and 0088 is 9b37b8b2 (built after both edits; the threshold sweep and lite5/lite6 ran with it: lite 15.8 / 16.9 s to the index mark vs 15.3-15.65 s with 58cec244 earlier, i.e. no measurable gain from 0087, no breakage). Committed to the local prebuilts clone `~/apklayer-build/prebuilts` as a71f9dbf (not pushed: no GitHub credentials here), lock row in `deps/android-tree-files-x86_64.lock` updated.
- 0087: no errno swap for `pthread_*` and `__errno`; one `__errno_location` call instead of two in the swap. Next: measure the load time before/after in `endfield-load`, then look at the guest-side cost of the trampoline.

## 2026-11-25: The AOT cache was never rebuilt after a runtime update (CdsDump.trainSpare)

- Cause: `trainSpare` returned when ANY `*.aot.log` existed in the instance's cds directory ("one attempt per instance"). The cache key hashes the runtime build, so after the first cache (an old `78d5...aot.log` from 2026-11-18) every later key found a log and never trained: spares ran in `-XX:AOTMode=record` for nothing (each wrote a 100-300 MB `.aotconf.*`; 8.8 GB piled up in one test session), took about 9 s to prepare, and cold starts ran without the cache.
- Fix: the guard looks for this key's own log (`<cache>.log`) only. Tried on the NVIDIA PC with a host-classes.jar that has the one class replaced (a new key): the spare trained once and the cache was made (141 MB, the stale one removed by the create step).
- Aurora Store, first frame, before -> after: cold stack 5.3 s -> 4.9 s (app loader 1.05 s -> 0.83 s); relaunch right after a stop 4.3-4.6 s -> 3.9 s (the spare is ready after about 1 s instead of 9 s; the target arrived 1.2 s after the launch instead of 1.9 s). Spare ready and idle: 2.2 s as before.
- Not changed: spares of different packages still replace each other (a spare is one app's), so a stack start with many components keeps starting and ending spares until it settles; each ended recording spare leaves its `.aotconf.*` until the next one removes it (10 minutes).

## 2026-11-26: YouTube's blank gear sheet, description, comments and Home feed: libcore.io.Memory had no natives
- Cause (ten agents, then probes in an own instance): the 465 empty rows were Litho `LazilyConvertedElement`s whose Element (6 KB of real bytes each) converted to an empty component (`vjk.e`: "Element missing type extension"). `wjt` (YouTube's Element over a native upb message) reads the has-bits and fields with `libcore.io.Memory.peekByte/peekLong` at the message's address; Robolectric instruments `libcore.io.Memory` and nothing bound `$$robo$$peekByte$nativeBinding` and the rest, so every peek returned 0 (probe: Unsafe read 3, Memory.peekByte read 0 at the same address). Only com.android.i18n.timezone.internal.Memory had natives (bridge/native/i18n_memory.c).
- Fix: `ShadowHostMemory` (runtime/host, registered in HostShadowProvider for libcore.io.Memory): peek/poke byte, short, int, long and the array forms (with `swap`) over sun.misc.Unsafe, the same address space as the JNI libraries. After it the probe reads 3, `wbe.f()/g()` are true, the type extensions resolve (168777401, 183314536) and the rows measure 660x555, 660x196, 660x142 (was 660x0).
- Test: `MemoryChecks` in tests/apps/hello-runtime (group runtime-identity): peekByte/peekLong/peekInt(swap)/peekByteArray/pokeInt against Unsafe memory. Compiled, not run. Not checked by eye: the run's screenshots showed the consent page.
- Tried and dropped: registering the same natives in the C shim under `$$robo$$` names made JNI_OnLoad fail (the class FindClass found does not carry them): the Java shadow is the route.

## 2026-11-25: Play Store updates failed (gRPC UNKNOWN): non-main threads read SystemClock behind the monotonic clock

- Symptom: downloads worked, installing an update did not (`A/Finsky: Unexpected exception: StatusRuntimeException: UNKNOWN` at "Local install scheduled"). Cause in the app log: `IllegalArgumentException: duration (-0.137s) must not be negative` in gRPC's SerializingExecutor: Robolectric's paused SystemClock moves only on main-looper steps, so a stamp from System.nanoTime on one thread and a SystemClock reading on another gave a negative duration. Fix: `ShadowHostSystemClock` returns max(paused, System.nanoTime()) on threads other than main (64cc20af).
- Checked on the owner's default instance (patched copy of runtime 0.5.6's host-classes.jar): Endfield "(re)installed version 71" through Play Store, no "must not be negative", no Play Integrity (-100) or "Last device integrity refresh attempt failed" lines after the restart (the earlier -100 and integrity-refresh errors were probably the same bug in other gRPC calls; not forced by an app asking for an integrity token). Cronet "native library failed to load" (OkHttp fallback) not investigated.

## 2026-11-23: Endfield's scrambled tiles: the cause is the tiled GBM buffer on AMD; render buffers are LINEAR now (AMD, Intel)

- Cause found, not the textures: Endfield's first uploads (21 splash screens, 1920x1080 ASTC 4x4, dumped with APKLAYER_VULKAN_BLOCK_DUMP) decode cleanly with astcenc, Mesa's decoder matched astcenc on all 56 real-content probe cases, and the splash screen itself came out scrambled on screen, on Mesa 25.3.6 (ernstp PPA) and 26.2.7 (kisak) alike, with three different decoders. With `APKLAYER_GFX_LINEAR=1` (every GPU-render buffer an explicit LINEAR GBM buffer) the title screen is clean (mp100, RADV Renoir, 3440x1440).
- Reading: Mesa's GBM exports its implicit tiled layout with no modifier and the importers (Vulkan HAL swapchain images, shell, SurfaceFlinger) take that as LINEAR with GBM's pitch. graphics.c already had a workaround for AMD under ANGLE (made LINEAR only when GBM's pitch differs from the linear one), which does not catch a tiled layout with the same pitch.
- Change (bridge/hals/graphics/graphics.c): GPU-render buffers on amdgpu and i915/xe are created LINEAR by default; `APKLAYER_GFX_LINEAR=0` turns it off, `=1` forces it on any GPU (NVIDIA's GBM refuses LINEAR render targets and keeps its own layout, the code only swaps a buffer when the linear one was made). `APKLAYER_GFX_DEBUG=1` logs each AMD render buffer's GBM modifier and stride next to the linear stride. Not checked: Intel (no machine), the earlier note that always-LINEAR made 3072x1920 ANGLE windows black on AMD (Endfield at 3440x1440 is fine); the performance of linear render targets.
- mp100 (the owner's test PC): runtime/0.5.6/libapklayer-hal-graphics.so is now a local copy of the build (the deb's symlink is kept beside it as .link-before-linear-20261123); the Vulkan HAL there is the Mesa-decoder build (0849a3e8). Mesa on mp100 is the kisak PPA's 26.2.7 (the owner changed it).

- Owner: "fix the shimmering, also make renderscale minimum 65". Numbers in docs/FILTER-EVAL.md "Shimmer".
- Finding (RTX 5060 Ti, GLES): the filter is deterministic (identical frames give identical output, CMAA2 included) and its edge decisions do not flip: CMAA2 reduces the flicker of an aliased source (hair at 65 %: flick 28.99 FSR alone -> 26.83 with it; thresholds 0.025..0.1 and the colour term change nothing; more runs lower it further). Most of the crawl is the aliased source itself (bilinear alone 24.0 on hair); what the filter adds on top is EASU (reconstruction) and RCAS (sharpening of the aliasing: foliage flick 4.35 bilinear, 5.00 EASU, 6.76 EASU+RCAS, 6.34 default pipeline).

EASU is reference-exact apart from the earlier patches. Cost: a few ALU per pixel (no extra fetch).

- Not fixable by the filter: the flicker of an aliased source (a game without AA) moving by sub-pixel steps; only the game's own AA or a higher render scale removes it.

Findings on it: the edge thresholds (0.15..0.03), SMAA's local contrast adaptation (2.0..1.5) and CMAA2's local contrast, shape blur and dampening change nothing or only blur text as much as stairs; what smooths is more runs: the output of a run is the input of the next (stairs the first leaves get a second, longer look). Extra runs alone cost text (-0.07 text edge at 35 %), so they carry a text gate: the RCAS text test (sharpen_fsr.h) on the 3x3 removes the edges of text-like structure from the edge pass.
- CMAA2: levels now differ: threshold (.15/.10/.07/.05), colour edges (largest channel step x 0/0.4/0.5/0.6 joins the luma step), runs by upscale ratio (low 1, medium 2 from ratio 2, high round(ratio) max 3, ultra round(1.4 ratio) max 4: 4 at 35 %, 3 at 50 %, 2 at 75 %), the text gate (0.1) in every run (text edge up 0.02-0.04 against before). SMAA: medium uses colour edges, high runs twice from ratio 2.4, ultra twice from ratio 1.4 with corner rounding 40 (was 25), the text gate in the second run. The numbers are uniforms of one program per kernel (`u_th`, `u_ck`, `u_tg`; SMAA `smaa_th`, `smaa_lca`, `smaa_tg`); `smaa_run`/`cmaa_run` take the ratio. Table in docs/FILTER-EVAL.md. No setting added; GLES only (Vulkan still maps them to `high`). Own AA was not used (the owner is removing it).

## 2026-11-23: Endfield tiles: Mesa's ASTC decoder as an option (APKLAYER_VULKAN_ASTC_DECODER=mesa), build log

- waydroid-nvidia (github.com/Shiro836/waydroid-nvidia, MIT) decodes ASTC on desktop NVIDIA with Mesa's `astc_decoder.glsl` compute shader (the one anv/radv emulation uses), one pipeline per block size, in the app's command buffer at the buffer-to-image copy. The HAL takes that decoder as a third GPU variant: `TextureAstcMesa.cpp` (HAL side: LUT buffer and views, set layout, pipelines, per-image descriptor sets, dispatch of 2x2 blocks per workgroup) behind two hooks in gfxstream's `CompressedImageInfo` (`gMesaAstcHooks`, apklayer patches: decode in `decompress()`, forget in `destroy()`, SAMPLED usage on the block images, accessors); `mesa_astc/` holds Mesa's shader, Granite's LUT code (both MIT, unmodified) and the generated SPIR-V (glslang 11.8.0, recipe in mesa_astc/README). 3D images and any setup failure fall back to the gfxstream shader. Default (owner's decision, same day): Mesa's decoder on every driver, NVIDIA's proprietary one included (not yet tested there: the probe and PGR run on the NVIDIA PC next); `APKLAYER_VULKAN_ASTC_DECODER=new|old` selects gfxstream's per-pixel or per-block shader.
- Build log (`gsi_x86_64 userdebug`, incremental, `flock ~/los24-build.lock`, Mac ~/los24 via ssh): `m vulkan.apklayer` (existing module; a new static library `libapklayer_astc_luts` for the LUT code). Why: the new decoder variant above; nothing else builds the HAL.

## 2026-11-22 PGR crash: a proxy library's stub function lost its wrapper (binary_translation 0085)
- Cause, from the core of the crash (java pid 793151, 20:43:59): CRIWARE's first `slCreateEngine(&engine, 0, NULL, 0, NULL, NULL)` (libcri_ware_unity.so +0xd05c8, from Unity's managed audio init) called the guest libOpenSLES.so, a berberis proxy stub (3 four-byte function stubs, `slCreateEngine` at 0x4080 = `b -0x40` to a `mov x3,#0; blr x3` placeholder). The stub's wrapper entry in the translation cache (made at load by `native_bridge_intercept_symbol` -> `InterceptGuestSymbol` -> `MakeTrampolineCallable`) was gone: the cache entry of that pc was kEntryNotTranslated and `berberis_GetDispatchAddress` returned 0 (`jmp *%rcx`, rcx = 0, in `berberis_entry_Interpret`). `TranslationCache::InvalidateGuestRange` drops EVERY entry in a range, wrappers too (`entry->host_code->store(kEntryNotTranslated); erase`), and it is called by `IcIvau` (a guest instruction-cache invalidate) and `GuestMapShadow::ClearExecutable` (a protection change): nothing makes a dropped wrapper again, so the stub's raw placeholder runs. Intermittent (a later run called `slCreateEngine` fine), PGR has an anti-cheat that touches code pages; also two of today's three PGR cores are in OpenSL ES creation (17:43: a mutex assert in libwilhelm).
- Fix (patches/aosp/frameworks/libs/binary_translation/0085-keep-intercepted-stubs.patch): `InterceptGuestSymbol` remembers every function it wrapped (library, name, first instruction word); `berberis_HandleNotTranslated` first calls `RestoreInterceptedGuestSymbol(pc)`, which wraps it again if the first word is still the stub's (so freed-and-reused addresses are not hijacked); `berberis_GetDispatchAddress` and `ExecuteGuest` treat a zero cache entry as kEntryNotTranslated instead of jumping to it.
- Build log (`gsi_x86_64 userdebug`, incremental, `flock -n ~/los24-build.lock`, Mac OrbStack VM ~/los24 via `ssh erfanabdi@100.85.219.120`): `APKLAYER_NATIVE_BRIDGE=arm64 breakfast gsi_x86_64 userdebug && m libberberis_arm64` (existing module; four edited files, no new source file). ## 2026-11-22 the anti-aliasing works on 3D scenes (colour-aware edges, a second pass)
- The owner: the anti-aliasing is not applied to 3D stuff. Cause: `FS_AA` took its edge strength and direction from luma only and started at a luma contrast of 0.05 (full strength at 0.25): a 3D scene's edges are low in contrast or differ in hue only, so the old pass did next to nothing there (measured stair roughness, hue-only edges, ratio 2: 16.02 off, 15.95 old high). Now (`FS_AA`, sharpen_more.h): the edge strength is the largest colour step to a neighbour (any channel), the direction comes from the structure tensor of the three channels' Sobel gradients, the ramp is 0.015..0.08 (was 0.05..0.25 luma); at the high level and ratio >= 1.5 the pass runs twice, the second at half strength (`post_run`).
- Measured (SGSR, aliased point-sampled sources, 1280x720, stair roughness off -> new high; PSNR vs the full picture off -> new high): strong edges ratio 2: 53.3 -> 34.9 (36.06 -> 37.02 dB), ratio 2.86: 42.7 -> 25.0 (36.18 -> 37.59); hue-only edges ratio 2: 16.0 -> 11.4 (46.69 -> 47.39), 2.86: 11.4 -> 7.7; low-contrast ratio 2: 7.78 -> 6.70 (52.90 -> 53.59), 2.86: 6.28 -> 5.37; the game-like picture with text: ratio 2 67.6 -> 54.9 (31.40 -> 31.60 dB), 2.86 56.5 -> 41.2 (30.44 -> 30.50). Cost: a source that is already smooth loses PSNR (high: 37.64 -> 35.15, low 37.17): `render-aa low` or `off` for games that have their own AA. A full second pass at the same strength smoothed text too much (31.30 dB at ratio 2, below no AA) and was not kept.

## 2026-11-22 the shell no longer freezes on an app that stops reading its socket
- The owner: resizing PGR on GLES 'froze, PGR just crashes'. Five investigations (core dump, logs, code reading, a resize stress test of the GLES filter, the Wayland protocol side): the PGR java process crashed FIRST by itself at 20:43:59 (berberis: a guest call through a null pointer, guest pc in a read-only page of libOpenSLES, host_pc 0, Unity's render thread inside `nativeRender`; `hs_err_pid793151.log`) and then spent 92 s writing a 541 MB core with its socket still open and unread. The shell kept sending it input events with a BLOCKING write on its single thread: the 20:44:48 core of apklayer-shell shows `write(fd 9, 24 bytes)` (a hover event) asleep in the kernel (rax = -ERESTARTSYS), the shell stopped answering xdg_wm_base pings, KWin's `kwin_killer_helper` ("not responding") ran and killed the shell with a plain `kill(pid, SIGABRT)` (si_code SI_USER, siginfo of the core). The GLES filter survived a resize stress run (random output and input sizes every 1-3 frames, modes 0-4, with ASAN and GL error checks: no failure, no fd or memory growth); no Wayland protocol error is involved.
- Fix (`client_send`, `client_flush` in bridge/shell/client.c, the poll set in main.c): every send to an app is MSG_DONTWAIT. Input and vsync messages that find the socket full are dropped; configure, release and the other messages wait in a per-client queue (256 KB cap, order kept) that is flushed when the socket drains (POLLOUT); the shell logs once when an app stops reading and when it reads again. Tested on a socket pair with a reader that never reads: 2000 input sends cost 2 ms in total (worst 0.02 ms), 50 queued releases arrived in order after the reader drained.
- Not fixed: the PGR crash itself (berberis guest fault near libOpenSLES, docs/PLAN.md).

## 2026-11-22: exclusive-monitor epochs (patch 0084), build log

- Build log (`gsi_x86_64 userdebug`, incremental, `flock ~/los24-build.lock`, Mac ~/los24): `APKLAYER_NATIVE_BRIDGE=arm64 breakfast gsi_x86_64 userdebug && m libberberis_arm64` (existing module; one new header, no new source file). Why: run 11's `locks` phase shows LDXR/STXR losing nodes to ABA (35% of the pops).
- Patch 0084: `runtime_primitives/exclusive_epoch.h` (a 16 KB table of counters below 2 GB, indexed by address bits 4..13); interpreter and lite tier: LDXR reads the counter before the value and keeps it in the upper half of cpu.reservation_value, STXR fails when it moved and bumps it on success; the heavy tier bails on LDXR/STXR so such regions stay lite-translated. LDXP/STXP (pairs) are unchanged.
- Result: the first design (counter checked before the CAS, bumped after it) cut the lost nodes of the llsc64 phase from 1126640/1141852 to 373719/23920; the remaining window (CAS done, bump pending) was closed by doing check, CAS and bump under a per-entry lock (a 64-bit lock word beside the 32-bit counter; the assembler has Xchgq with a memory operand, not Xchgl; the lock is released on a fault too). Two builds failed on that way (Xchgl), the third passed: `locks` on the NVIDIA PC (private instance, private APKLAYER_ANDROID_LIBS copy with the new library, 3 s stress): PASS, `llsc64 double_owned plain=0 delay=0`, every other count 0.
- PGR on mp100 with the new library (replacing the translator in runtime/0.5.6/android-libs, original kept as libberberis_arm64.so.orig-20261122), normal fast mode, owner-run: the download went past 20 GB at full speed without a lock error or stall (before: a stall after 1.8 to 6.3 GB, within 2-3 minutes). The interpret-only run (slow, 4 MB/s) also passed 9 GB, as the speed theory predicted. So the ABA in LDXR/STXR was the cause of the PGR download stall.
- Prebuilts: x86_64 `libberberis_arm64.so` faf1b252 (was b59d5c1f) committed in the local prebuilts clone `~/apklayer-deb-hubfix/prebuilts` as 397b84a (with a MANIFEST line), not pushed (no GitHub credentials here). The next deb built from that clone carries it; a runtime bundle release also needs `tools/release/versions` bumped (docs/RELEASES.md).
- Not yet: the cost of the lock in STXR-heavy code; the unit tests of the lite/interpreter exclusives in the AOSP tree (not run); LDXP/STXP are unchanged.

## 2026-11-22: PGR download stall, run 11: the translator's LDXR/STXR is ABA-unsafe (locks group now fails)

- Candidate from an offline review of patches 0024/0033: LDXR/STXR are modelled as a compare-and-swap of the value (reservation address + loaded value), so a store of the same value by another thread does not clear the monitor, as arm64 does. The old `locks` stack test is tagged (128-bit pointer + counter), so it could not see it.
- New phase in `tests/apps/hello-arm64/locks.c`: an untagged 64-bit LL/SC stack (12 nodes, 8 threads, 400000 pop/own/release/push each; `ldaxr head; ldr next,[head]; stlxr`), plain and with 16 nops between the load and the store. Built on the Mac (build.sh, package renamed to hello.llsc so the installed hello.arm64 stays), run on the NVIDIA PC in its own instance `llsc` (removed afterwards), 3 s stress: `llsc64 double_owned plain=1126640 delay=1141852` of 3200000 ops each (35%); the 128-bit stacks 0. On real arm64 it is 0 (any store to the head by another thread clears the monitor).
- So a lock-free list written with LL/SC loses nodes to ABA here: two threads own one block, the double free of 32-byte blocks and the recycled monitor that fits the lock errors. Not yet shown that IL2CPP's free list (guest 0xaa2c070) is a single-word LL/SC stack; its code is in the dumps of run 7.
- `tests/vm/locks.sh` (group `locks`) fails until the translator is fixed. Also seen in that run: handler_outside=1 sp_outside=1 (not looked into; the old phases were all 0 before).
- Fix idea (not done): a per-granule epoch table bumped by every successful STXR, checked with the value compare under a small lock in STXR (covers stores through exclusives, the shape of such lists; plain stores to the word stay unseen). Interpreter, lite and heavy tiers all need it.
- Cleaned: Mac ~/apklayer-llsc-test, this PC ~/apklayer-llsc, the instance llsc and its test app.

- Two runs of Endfield on wesley-mp100 (instance default, `nice -n 10`, about 45 s each, stopped with `apklayer stop <pkg>`), `APKLAYER_VULKAN_TEXTURE_TRACE=1` and `=nodecode`, screenshots of the app's own picture (3440x1440).

The display sink's log said `acquireBuffer: max acquired buffer count reached: 7 (max 6)`: an app sends a burst of 7 frames at its start and the sink holds every presented buffer until the shell gives it back; the first frame included ~90 ms of EGL/shader setup, so no buffer went back in time, the 7th acquire failed, its frame stayed queued with nothing to retry it, and SurfaceFlinger and the app blocked for good. Now: the pass is prepared in a helper thread (`sharpen_prepare`), the first frames take the normal path (their dmabufs are kept as dups), the main loop (`sharpen_win_poll`) imports them when the helper is done and shows the picture on screen again through the pass; a drawn buffer goes back at once (the sink's release takes the lock its present path holds while it records the frame: no race), a replaced waiting frame too; a full ring of three output buffers keeps the newest frame waiting for the compositor's release instead of showing the soft one. NVIDIA's gbm has no linear render target (RENDERING|LINEAR fails; with the compositor's tiled modifier 0x300000000e08014 it works), so there it needs a compositor that lists a tiled modifier. The notes below about the shell doing the scaling are the first version.

- Compositors: GNOME and KDE have wp_viewporter, so any percent works there. Without it (an old Mir, Lipstick's wl_shell) the shell can show a buffer only at a whole multiple of the logical size, so a render scale whose result is not a whole multiple (25..99, 125, 150...) is ignored there, once logged in shell.log ("render scale N% ignored"); 200% still works. Written, NOT run (no GNOME Shell test VM here).

## 2026-11-21: dex2jvm splits methods inside a try range whose handlers are copied (MindTheGapps x86_64 Play Store and Play services)

- MindTheGapps x86_64's Play Store 30.4.17 failed to start ("Failed to initialize FinskyApp": qeb.d()V needs code_length 109416) and its Play
  services 22.21.16's persistent process crashed (deaq.<clinit> 104564): both methods were oversize stubs. qeb.d (25,828 code units) has one
  try range over 98% of it, so MethodSplitter found no legal cut ("no valid cut within 65187 bytes"), and its handlers (`throw new
  AssertionError("Could not parse proto flag ...")`, no move-exception) could not be cloned either.
- MethodSplitter (replan only): a handler without move-exception may be cloned (the copy pops the exception, as the handler stub does), and so
  may a deferred `new` with its own <init> inside the copy; a range whose every handler is cloned may be cut, each part keeping its piece of
  the range (Translator.assignPartTries clips the ranges to the part) with its own handler copy. Methods the first plan already split come out
  unchanged; only methods that used to be stubbed are affected.
- Test (NVIDIA PC): standalone dex2jvm on both APKs: qeb.d and deaq.<clinit> in 3 parts each, no stub left; the owner's default instance
  reconverted with it: Play Store launches (owner), and in a test instance it reaches MainActivity.

## 2026-11-21: the hub stays answerable when a provider's process hangs; a window closed at the splash ends its launch

- Provider lookups (owner's Play services hang, entry below): a provider the process installed at its start is handed to the hub from the endpoint's
  binder thread (HubEndpoint.INSTALLED, filled by AppEnvironment.installProviders), as Android's published providers need no main thread; one
  created on first use waits for the main thread at most 20 s (CONTENT_PROVIDER_WAIT_TIMEOUT), then none. The hub's binder pool is system_server's
  31 threads instead of an app's 8 (RealBinder.startPool1, `apklayer.binderthreads`; a shim without it keeps 8, registered on its own so
  older host classes still load).
- Early close: a CLOSE that reaches the window sink (the app has not taken the window yet) sends SIGTERM to the launcher named by
  `APKLAYER_CLOSE_ENDS` when it is the sink's parent (bridge/hals/graphics/display.c, set by cli/run.cpp); the launcher keeps a signal that comes
  before its JVM exists and hands it over (passSignalsTo(0)). Before, the JVM ran on without a window and the next launch went to it.
- Tests (NVIDIA PC, tree rebased on origin/main 4d481799, built and installed against the upstream prebuilts e8904ab with a private
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/data/state home, so the owner's apklayerd and apps were not used): providers basic denied death idle and the new `stuck` (the
  provider's main thread sleeps 40 s; 12 lookups of its other authorities and a Settings read answer in 21 ms; without the HubEndpoint change
  TimeoutException) pass; activities (all 11) and the new tests/vm/early-close.py pass (the run ends at once, no JVM left; the deb's CLI ran on 15 s
  and more); devices.sh: `tethering supported=false in 7 ms`, then "not exactly one network" (this PC has tailscale0 beside Ethernet).
  Not exercised: the 20 s wait of a provider created on first use; the 31-thread pool on its own (the stuck test passes through the fast path).

  first failed to compile (necessary: Venus-allocated swapchain memory in Driver.cpp, the fence-fd report; a one-file module, nothing else rebuilt; the

- Evidence (tests/vm/venus-export-probe.c on the UTM VM, Venus 'Apple M5 Max' + virgl on one renderD128): (1) a dma-buf Venus allocates and exports (buffer
  or explicit-LINEAR image memory, VkExportMemoryAllocateInfo DMA_BUF) is imported by virgl's EGL (EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import) and sampled: the Vulkan
  GPU clear (vkCmdClearColorImage, sync_fd semaphore signalled in time) reads back exactly. It must be a HOST_VISIBLE memory type: type 0 (device-local only)
  imports but reads GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY. (2) the other direction, a GBM (virgl) bo imported into Venus: vkAllocateMemory and vkBindImageMemory succeed, the first
  submit that uses the image aborts (exit 134): the known limit, reproduced standalone (`venus-export-probe export|import`).
- Cause of the stuck first present: the gralloc buffers of a swapchain are virgl's (the allocator's GBM), Venus aborts or never completes on them (not a missing
  signal in our present path). Fix (Driver.cpp allocateExported): on Venus the image memory at the first acquire is allocated by Venus
  (dedicated, exportable), exported with vkGetMemoryFdKHR and dup3'd over the gralloc handle's fd number, so the compositor attaches the Venus buffer
  (same size, stride and modifier: the image keeps the gralloc buffer's explicit linear layout). Memory type: the first HOST_VISIBLE one of the image.
- ANGLE (Vulkan) on Venus: (a) the app crashed at pc 0 in the Android loader's PresentOneSwapchain: the loader offers VK_EXT_swapchain_maintenance1
  when sync fds import into fences (Venus reports it) but loads vkImportFenceFdKHR only for a device that lists VK_KHR_external_fence_fd (Venus does not):
  Driver.cpp reports the sync-fd fence import absent then (vkGetPhysicalDeviceExternalFenceProperties), and the host fence import is no longer used there.
  (b) SurfaceFlinger then aborted (signal 6, "Enter boot animation"): with ANGLE on Vulkan the compositor's Linux ANGLE imports the buffers the allocator made
  (virgl), the same Venus limit. cli/env.cpp: on a Venus host the apps get ANGLE on Vulkan, the compositor and the buffer transfers stay on the native EGL
  (APKLAYER_ANGLE_GLES=vulkan, the GLES mode's wiring; stack.cpp writes the Vulkan backend props). `hostVulkan` no longer skips Venus (it keeps a ` venus`
  flag in its cache file).
- Tests on the UTM VM (own tree, JDK 25, prebuilts 99acf395 + the rebuilt vulkan.apklayer.so): vulkan-present now PASS on Venus (600 frames, 93% of the
  window magenta in the screenshot; the Venus skip is gone), gpu, gpu-window, window-formats, vulkan, vulkan-textures, vulkan-select, texture-view, fences,

## 2026-11-21: ANGLE on Mesa (Intel UHD 630 and AMD Navi 14, MacBookPro16,1): the app crash fixed (branch anglefix2)
- Root cause: ANGLE creates its swapchain with VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_DEFERRED_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_BIT_EXT. The Android loader then calls `vkCreateImage` with a `VkImageSwapchainCreateInfoKHR` naming its own `Swapchain` object (swapchain.cpp, deferred branch); the HAL forwards that to the host driver, whose WSI code dereferences the handle as its own swapchain (Mesa: a NULL VkDevice inside, `jmp *0x500(%rdi)`, SIGSEGV on the RenderThread ~4 s after ANGLE starts). The crash frame's rdi was Mesa's, not the loader's `device`. Fix: `patches/aosp/frameworks/native/0010-vulkan-host-no-deferred-swapchain-memory.patch` (the loader allocates the buffers up front over a host driver, the flag is only permission to defer).
- AMD under ANGLE (`bridge/hals/graphics/graphics.c`): GBM reports no modifier for GPU-render buffers and the Vulkan HAL / ANGLE's EGL import read that as LINEAR with GBM's pitch (161 px: 1024 B, RADV: 768, GFX10 needs equal pitches): `VK_ERROR_INVALID_DRM_FORMAT_MODIFIER_PLANE_LAYOUT_EXT` for hardware-bitmap pictures (HWUI's AImageReader), and SurfaceFlinger died on a resized window (`eglCreateImageKHR` EGL_BAD_PARAMETER). Buffers whose GBM pitch differs from the LINEAR one are now allocated LINEAR (equal pitches keep GBM's layout: always LINEAR made the 3072x1920 windows black).
- `cli/layout.cpp`: a source tree's ANGLE libraries come from the install prefix (`layout.angle`), so tree-based ANGLE tests work; `tests/vm/gpu-smoke.py`: under ANGLE the capture is taken 4 s after ANGLE starts and SurfaceFlinger's log must show 3 imported buffers.
- Groups with APKLAYER_GLES_ANGLE=on, `tests/run -j 1` (parallel runs gave false failures), compositor log `compositor EGL: Linux ANGLE (Vulkan)` on both. AMD: gpu (HARDWARE copy read back, pictures 20/20), gpu-window, gles1, texture-view, vulkan, vulkan-present, exit-clean, gfx-readback pass; gl-formats (its offscreen btload half runs outside a stack, no ANGLE property: libEGL finds no driver; the window half: fails=0), fences (EGL_ANDROID_get_frame_timestamps is unsupported under ANGLE; the fence checks themselves pass), window-formats (10-bit: red and blue swapped, fp16: black) fail. Intel: the same set, plus gpu hwbitmap, with the same four groups failing (gpu-window passed once warm; its first run in a fresh instance stalled 3 s: the cold-start effect also behind AMD's one-off TextureView stall). ANGLE off on both GPUs: window-formats passes with all six configs including fp16-opaque and 10-bit-opaque, no "Stride didn't match" line (mapper.apklayer fix); gl-formats, fences, gpu-window pass.
- Zero copy (strace -f -y, glbench window clear 6 s, app JVM and SurfaceFlinger; ANGLE on): no mmap, read, write or DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC on any dma-buf, no glReadPixels, no "ANGLE GPU CPU-map path" line, on either GPU. AMD (360 frames): app 737 poll()s on sync_file fds (2.0 per frame, 3000 ms timeout), 1482 DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT + 1113 TIMELINE_WAIT (GPU syncobj waits, 7 per frame), 24 GEM mmaps in the whole run; SurfaceFlinger 2558 sync_file polls with timeout 0 (7 per frame, status checks), 365 AMDGPU_CS, 9 PRIME_FD_TO_HANDLE (its imports). Intel (188 frames, 31 fps under strace): app 393 sync_file polls (2.1 per frame), SurfaceFlinger 1515 (8 per frame, timeout 0).
- Open: ANGLE 10-bit windows swap red and blue and fp16 windows are black (both GPUs); fences needs EGL_ANDROID_get_frame_timestamps under ANGLE; gl-formats' offscreen run needs the ANGLE property outside a stack; AMD's LINEAR buffers are slower than tiled/DCC ones (modifiers.c's explicit list for Mesa is the way); app-created images with VkImageSwapchainCreateInfoKHR still reach the host driver with the loader's handle; NVIDIA now takes the eager swapchain path too (not run).

## 2026-11-21: Play services hung in isTetheringSupported, and the instance with it

- Seen on the NVIDIA PC (owner's default instance, deb 0.5.2+local): Play Store stayed on its splash and later launches never came up; apps
  with Google Play services started slowly or not at all. Thread dumps (SIGQUIT): Play services' main thread waited in
  `ConnectivityManager.isTetheringSupported` -> `TetheringManager.RequestDispatcher.waitForResult` (`ConditionVariable.block(60 s)` on the app's
  clock, which stands while the main thread waits: 17 h), right after its AppCertService started. Robolectric's fake "tethering" service answered
  the call but never called the `IIntResultListener`. With that main thread gone, provider lookups into Play services held 8 of the hub's 9 binder
  threads (`HubProviders.find`), so the hub answered nothing else: Play Store's `Settings.Secure.getString` (HostLocation.install) and
  YouTube's `cancelJob` waited for ever.
- Fix: a fake service call that carries an `IIntResultListener` (tethering's result callback) answers it at once with TETHER_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED,
  as a device without tethering does (ShadowHostServiceManager.wrap). hello-devices prints `isTetheringSupported`; tests/vm/devices.sh expects false.
- Test (NVIDIA PC, own instance, stock runtime 0.5.0 with the tree's host-classes.jar): hello.devices with the stock jar never got past the call
  in 20 s (no PASS); with the fix `tethering supported=false in 7 ms`, PASS. `tests/run devices` not run (no test VM configured on this PC).

## 2026-11-20: Vulkan HAL: VK_ANDROID_external_memory_android_hardware_buffer (hardware bitmaps under ANGLE)

- New `aosp/hals/graphics/vulkan/HardwareBuffer.cpp`: vkGetAndroidHardwareBufferPropertiesANDROID from our gralloc handle (dma-buf size,
  vkGetMemoryFdPropertiesKHR types, VkFormat and the host's features at the buffer's modifier), vkCreateImage of an AHardwareBuffer image
  with the buffer's explicit DRM layout, vkAllocateMemory importing its dma-buf (dedicated), and the AHardwareBuffer handle type answered in
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2. Advertised where the host has external_memory_fd, dma_buf, image_drm_format_modifier and
  queue_family_foreign, not on Venus. Shortcut: the image takes the layout of the last properties query of the same size on its thread (ANGLE
  and Skia always query right before they create). No YUV external formats, no export.
- Build log: sync aosp/hals/graphics/vulkan to the Mac tree, `m vulkan.apklayer` (gsi_x86_64 userdebug), incremental, flock; a new source
  file, so Soong regenerates its graph: two builds (11:42, then with diagnostics), both succeeded; x86_64 output f07e7aeb (first build).
- First run: ANGLE enabled the extension (log `VK_ANDROID_external_memory_android_hardware_buffer on device`), but the hardware bitmap's
  buffer had modifier 0x300000000e08014: NVIDIA's GBM picks a compressed block-linear kind (c=1, kind 0x08) for a render+sample buffer.
  NVIDIA's EGL lists 6 compressed and 6 uncompressed tiled modifiers for AB24, its Vulkan driver only the 6 uncompressed ones
  (0x300000000606010-15), so no Vulkan image could use the buffer.
- Allocator (bridge/hals/graphics/modifiers.c, new): tiled gralloc buffers on NVIDIA are made with gbm_bo_create_with_modifiers2 from EGL's
  uncompressed block-linear modifiers (Linux ANGLE's list in an ANGLE instance, already Vulkan's); other GPUs list none and keep GBM's
  choice. readback.c's EGL modifier query is shared (apklayer_gfx_egl_modifiers).
- Checked on the RTX 5060 Ti, hello-hwbitmap (built on the Mac) in a throwaway instance with a symlinked runtime copy: before, ANGLE on:
  `copy config null`, `Could not create EGL image`. After, ANGLE on and off: `copy config HARDWARE`, `readback ff0000ff ffff8000`,
  `crops 50/50`, `pictures 20/20`, ImageDecoder/BitmapFactory/decodeStream/decodeResource HARDWARE (tests/vm/hwbitmap.py's checks).
  Not checked: YouTube itself; `apklayer screenshot` of this app is black in native mode and fails in ANGLE mode with the stock runtime too
  (not this change). Deleted afterwards: the instance, the app, `~/apklayer-hwbitmap-{rt,libs}` (3.4 MB), the Mac's build script and log.

## 2026-11-20: Endfield on NVIDIA: window buffers get their memory at vkCreateImage (GPU fault fixed)

- Endfield (owner's runtime, vulkan.apklayer eb1b4a59): the login dialog over a black screen; the kernel logs `Xid 31` (UnityMain, MMU fault
  at 0x4000, GPCCLIENT_PROP) and the HAL `QueueSignalReleaseImageANDROID failed: -4` (device lost) right after the ASTC decoder starts.
  Reproduced (2 of 2 with the emulation, 0 of 1 without; without it Unity fails `vkCreateImage` of its 1920x1080 ASTC 4x4 image, vk -3).
- nvidia-prolapse (Waydroid NVIDIA, where Endfield works) notes NVIDIA 615.71.09 accepts an ASTC vkCreateImage and reports size 0.
- `APKLAYER_VULKAN_TEXTURE_TRACE=1` (TextureEmulation.cpp/TextureCommands.cpp): each emulated image's creation, memory requirements, bind,
  uploads and decodes, and any image with size-0 requirements. Host test vulkan-textures-test passes with it on.
- Not the emulation: with `APKLAYER_VULKAN_TEXTURE_TRACE=nodecode` (decoder skipped) the fault stayed; every emulated image had real sizes
  and binds. hello-vulkan's swapchain (600 frames, no views) presents fine.
- Cause, found with the Khronos validation layer (ANGLE's LinuxHost build, `VK_LAYER_PATH`): `VUID-VkImageViewCreateInfo-image-01020`, Unity
  makes views of its swapchain images before any memory is bound. Driver.cpp bound a window buffer's dma-buf only at the first

## 2026-11-18: Reuse virtual-display imports and map linear buffers directly

- Keep released DMA-BUF and Halium gralloc imports until their slot is needed. Reuse unused slots first, then replace the oldest released slot. Return old-size frames with their original fence before waiting on the GPU.

- Use synchronized DMA-BUF mappings for linear single-plane buffers when the exporter supports them. On the RTX 5060 Ti, median lock, write and unlock time on a 667×279 buffer was 8.72 µs to 7.91 µs with native EGL and 1,065 µs to 7.20 µs with ANGLE. The test read the expected pixels from the same exported buffer.

Keep sampling when the imported attachment is incomplete. The 667×279 tiled RGBA test verified pixels and padding at three pitches with native EGL and ANGLE. At 2680 bytes per row, median upload and readback improved from 1026 to 889 µs on native NVIDIA and from 1138 to 1014 µs on ANGLE.

## 2026-11-18: Follow the monitor and reduce frame waits

- The shell tracks refresh per Wayland output. Each window and its input client use their own output rate. The headless compositor clock uses the active window's output, so SurfaceFlinger can pace virtual displays on that clock.
- Replace the earlier virtual display queue rewrite with the original frame notifications. Wait on the acquire fence once outside the release lock, update geometry asynchronously, and return unshown Wayland buffers when a newer frame replaces them before configure.
- Reclaim released GBM buffers before the native GLES swap. Keep unsignaled buffers locked and block on a release only when GBM is out of free buffers. Cache native fence support for the process's GBM display.

## 2026-11-18: Keep virtual display releases moving during resize

- PGR hit the six-buffer acquire limit during a drag resize and then logged SurfaceFlinger commit timeouts. The virtual display's socket reader handled resize and release callbacks, but resize waited for a synchronous commit. The present thread also held the sink lock while `acquireBuffer` waited for a fence by default.
- Submit resize transactions without waiting for commit. Wait for the fence outside the sink lock and drain frames on either queue activity or a released slot. Stop acquiring at the configured limit so Wayland releases can resume pending work.

## 2026-11-17: Diagnose ANGLE GLES crash

- The crash reproduces with the project GLES 1 test app as well as AIDA64, and does not reproduce in AIDA64 with native GLES. ANGLE’s `GL_GetString` reads its current context from Android’s `TLS_SLOT_OPENGL`; on apklayer’s x86_64 host that TLS slot overlaps glibc’s `multiple_threads` field. Disable ANGLE’s Android TLS-slot optimization in the Android build, retain normal thread-local storage, rebuild x86_64/x86 and verify before packaging.

Next diagnostic build: x86_64 Android API 37 with `angle_enable_context_mutex=false`, to determine whether the invalid pointer is in ANGLE's context-lock path.
- `debug.renderengine.vulkan=true` made SurfaceFlinger avoid its Skia GLES initialization, so the Android services came up; the app's EGL loader then could not find `libEGL_angle.so`. The ANGLE driver paths must be added to the app JVM's system linker namespace as well as the initial process environment.
- Follow-up: the app JVM's `NativeLoader.init()` replaces the initial system linker path with `android-libs`, dropping the runtime's `android-root/system/lib{,64}` directory where ANGLE is linked. The driver must be reachable from EGL's app namespace.
- Follow-up correction: ANGLE is opened by EGL from the app namespace, so the driver dirs must be added to `NativeLoader`'s app path, not its system path. Build the host classes and smoke this adjustment with the Google ANGLE binaries.
- The active-mode environment guard did not make the directory visible to EGL. Detect the packaged runtime symlink instead and append its system library dirs to the app path whenever ANGLE is installed; rebuild host classes and smoke again.

## 2026-11-17: PGR agent VIRAPP: the ACE wait loop at VM 0x1d20c is a HIT on our own package; fix = no dummy 'android' application for JNI callers

- **Result.** VM 0x1d1c8 (the 'wait 30 or 600 s' loop polling +2d4994, a bool in the ACE singleton +0x2b0, 0 on both routes the whole run) is only entered when a scanner of VM 0x11290 (vtable 0xd6e8) reports a hit (this[0x49]=1, name at this+0x4a). Read live on the translated route the name is our OWN package. The scanner is 0x15148 ('uis_va'): candidates = package names cut from /proc/self/maps, fd and map_files lines under /data/data|/data/app|/data/user/0 ending .so/.apk, minus an own-name set (0x15310: the cached key 'package_name' via +2d216c, and the first line of /proc/<pid>/cmdline) and 'com.google*'; per candidate 0x17640 compares st_uid of /proc/<pid> and /data/data/<name> (equal = hit; the own package matches by construction). The cached key was 'android': ACE's static init calls ActivityThread.currentActivityThread().getApplication().getFilesDir()/getPackageName() and Robolectric's dummy initial application (package android) answered (getFilesDir threw 'No data directory found for package android'; a device answers null there). Natively the candidate list is empty (host paths in the raw maps), so the loop never runs. kvcache8 decodes (XOR with '0123456789ABCD..', records [u32 klen][key][u32 vlen][val]): '*#20250421.1'='0', 'is_history_x86'='0', 'vm_app_ver'='4.9.1.179267863': the 3rd record (97 B vs native 64 B) is written by VM 0x1d2a8 inside the hit path; no x86 detector fires on either route.
- **Fix (default off).** `ShadowHostActivityThread.getApplication()`: null for a caller from native code (first non-plumbing frame is a native method, or none) while only the dummy exists; Java callers unchanged (patch 0029's Java-wide null broke KrApplication's MMKV.initialize). Knob `-Dapklayer.noDummyApp=true` (APKLAYER_JOPTS).
- **Checked** (tester PC, fresh account-free pgrp5, private APKLAYER_NATIVE copy of runtime 0.4.19 with the new host-classes.jar): without the knob VM pc 0x1d20c at 40/60 s, kvcache8 97 B; with it VM pc 0x31c (native's tick loop) at 30/40/50/80/120 s, kvcache8 64 B, atti_obv.dat written, no 'invalid size' in 130 s (2 runs). Tools: /tmp scratch only (flag/state sampler, live ctx reader: real address of a VM pointer = VM region base + sign-extended 32-bit value).

## 2026-11-16: PGR agent M: what the freed pointers are; the chain does not need the trampoline; native never starts ACE's Tencent network stage; the native trampoline death is a stack-protector abort in the wrapper

- **The chain is not the trampoline's.** Preload rebuilt from main (3139e3b, no `vma_names.c`, `nm -D` shows no `pthread_create`) on the tester PC, used through a private `APKLAYER_NATIVE` dir of symlinks (checked: the game's maps show `~/pgr-m-build/libapklayer-preload.so`; `libberberis_arm64.so` sha 985ec9c9 at start and end; pgrshared, 40-60 s runs under the lock): 12 of 15 runs died at 32.5-39.8 s (connect :10012 at 25-31 s, 20-63 invalid frees right after, SIGBUS tgkill 6-8 s later), 3 outlived the 40-46 s limit (chance, as before). Same chain as with the trampoline.
- **The 0x1010-stride pointers** (`BERBERIS_LOG_FREES=1` plus `tools/ace/ace-malloc.bt`, a uprobe on the host glibc `malloc`/`calloc` for 4072..4104 bytes, joined with the refused-free lines of the same run, run 8): they are ACE's own 4096-byte `malloc` results (glibc chunk 0x1010) of the net thread, consecutive slots of one arena heap (a 64 MB-aligned `0x...58000000` region). The first refused pointers have `malloc(4096)` records of the net thread about 10 s before the storm (the others are not in the capture: allocated before the probe window or by another call); every one is "never freed by the guest in the last 65536 frees"; the header word at ptr-8 is a heap pointer, ASCII of /proc/self/maps lines or 0 (memory reused or freed and merged). So not an mmap/memfd/ioctl/getrandom/read product and not a translator allocation: the guest thunk (libanogs +0x1f5238, `blr x1`) calls host `free` on a table of stale slot pointers, as agent C found.
- **Native never starts that network stage.** AWS, private home `~/pgr-m-xdg` (copies of runtime/apps, overlay of `pgrtest/storage`, instance `pgrm`; libanogs sha equal on both hosts), plain main preload, `ace-net.bt`, 61 s run (rc 0): 0 connects to :10012, 0 to the Tencent IPs 101.32.143.* / 129.226.*; the game's connects are 47.236.252.113:50000, cloudflare :443, DNS, logdw. Translated runs reach the Tencent :443 stage at ~20 s and :10012 at 25-31 s in every dying run. So the first divergence found is not a syscall result but whether ACE enters its server stage at all (the earlier agent D table: a survivor had no game-thread sendto).
- **Native with the old trampoline also dies, but that is the wrapper's own abort, not ACE's verdict.** Main preload + `vma_names.c` (6e2704dd^) on `pgrm`: EXIT at 25.5, 28.4, 27.7 and 29.0 s after a SIGABRT self-tgkill (4 of 4). The aborting thread (clone3 chain 874445 -> 874671 -> 874775 -> 874776 in run 12) does rseq, set_robust_list, sched_getaffinity (pthread_getattr_np), `prctl(PR_SET_VMA)` (the stack naming), then `writev(2, ...)` of 44 bytes and tgkill: with `ace-stderr.bt` the iov is glibc's `*** %s ***: terminated` with 4 + 23 + 17 bytes, i.e. `*** stack smashing detected ***: terminated` from `named_start`'s own frame (it holds a `pthread_attr_t` and a 32-byte name, and calls `pthread_getattr_np`, `snprintf`, `free`) in a thread ACE created. The plain main preload on the same host and data lives (65.8 s rc 0, 46.7 s rc 0, 61.4 s rc 0). So agent H's fix (drop the trampoline) is right and says nothing about ACE's translated verdict; the lead's premise (the translated death is independent) stands. The stack-smash in the wrapper suggests ACE gives its threads tiny or hand-built stacks (a separate point: any wrapper that runs on an app thread must be stack-neutral).

Native survivors do them: plain-main run 1 and 14 ran the `cufsdosck`/`libc_malloc_debug_qemu`/`qemud`/`genyd` list (run 1 lived 65.8 s; run 14 ended at its own 25.9 s limit, no evidence), run 18 (lived 61 s) ran the `exagear`/`vbox86`/`android_x86`/`TGPAServer` list (39 hits), run 13 ran a zygisk list instead and lived 46.7 s. ## 2026-11-16: PGR on native arm64: main survives after 6e2704dd; the GL filter crash is a dlsym scope bug (agent K)
- AWS, main 6e2704dd built as a deb in a private tree, private home (pgrtest storage as an overlay), `tools/ace/pgr-timeline.sh`, true death, cap 100 s. Filter OFF (`glesFilterEnv` call removed): 5 of 5 alive (EXIT 100.6-101.7 s). A cold first run died at 46 s (microG "Cannot start com.google.android.gms for provider chimera", first start of a fresh home): not counted.
- Filter ON (main as is): 5 of 5 die 3-18 s after launch, SIGSEGV pc 0 in UnityMain (x0 = 0x91bf = GL_MAX_COMPUTE_WORK_GROUP_SIZE: `glGetIntegeri_v` pointer NULL).
- Cause (not a race): `cli/env.cpp` mapped libGLESv2.so/libGLESv3.so to the filter's absolute path. The file exists, so bionic_translation loads it with its own ELF loader (a soinfo); its glibc-loaded DT_NEEDED libGLESv2.so.2 has no soinfo and becomes libdl's (linker.c, "Dirty Hack Alarm"), and an app's dlsym on that handle (`apkenv_lookup_in_library`) walks soinfos only: every GL entry point the filter does not define itself returned NULL. Apps that fetch these through eglGetProcAddress never noticed.
- Fix: the cfg maps to the bare name `libapklayer_gles.so`: not in bionic's paths, so glibc's dlopen loads it (LD_LIBRARY_PATH holds the native dir) and glibc's dlsym searches its dependencies. Filter ON with the fix: 5 of 5 alive (EXIT 100.6-102.1 s); with `APKLAYER_GL_HIDE=GL_KHR_texture_compression_astc_ldr` 2 of 2 alive (99.0, 101.9 s; `APKLAYER_RUNTIME_DEBUG` shows the app's sampler queries going through the filter). Native arm64 PGR therefore survives on main 6e2704dd + this fix with the filter on.

## 2026-11-17: PGR: ACE's own-package hit fixed, on by default (ShadowHostContextImpl.getPackageName; for 0.5.1)

## 2026-11-16: Vulkan HAL: ASTC and ETC2/EAC emulated where the host device lacks them (Arknights: Endfield on NVIDIA)

- Endfield (Unity, owner's NVIDIA PC) creates a 1920x1080 `VK_FORMAT_ASTC_4x4_UNORM_BLOCK` image without asking (app log `vk result -3; ... format 157`); NVIDIA's (and AMD's) desktop drivers have neither ASTC nor ETC2. `vulkan.apklayer` now emulates both with gfxstream's emulation (the Android emulator's host code for the same gap, `host/vulkan/emulated_textures`, vendored unmodified with shims for its headers; docs/THIRD_PARTY.md): the app's image is an uncompressed image of the decoded format (RGBA8, R16/RG16 for EAC), each mip level's blocks live in a block-per-texel image beside it in the same memory, copies to/from the image go to those, and a barrier that makes the image readable runs gfxstream's compute decoder (ASTC to RGB, the ETC2/EAC shaders). The physical-device queries report the features and the decoded formats' features (gfxstream's masks); vkCreateDevice no longer asks the host for them.
- Ours beside gfxstream's (aosp/hals/graphics/vulkan/TextureEmulation.cpp, TextureCommands.cpp): a synchronization2 barrier of an emulated image decodes too (gfxstream passes those through undecoded); the app's compute pipeline, descriptor sets and push constants of the command buffer are bound again after the decoder (gfxstream rebinds the first two); dedicated allocation is never asked for an emulated image (its memory holds the block images too); a format list or ASTC decode-mode struct naming the compressed format is left out of the host's create calls. Only a device whose physical device lacks the feature is touched; `APKLAYER_VULKAN_TEXTURE_EMULATION=0` turns it off, `=force` emulates everywhere (tests).
- Test: new group `vulkan-textures` (`tests/hals/vulkan-textures-test.cpp`, built by Meson against the host loader as `vulkan-select-test` is): the entry points called as Android's loader calls them on the host's GPU; features/format queries report ASTC, an 8x8 ASTC 4x4 image with two mip levels gets five void-extent blocks, decodes at the readable barrier, its texels (exact colours, both levels) and its blocks read back; once with version-1 barriers and copies, once with synchronization2. Passes on the NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti (driver 615.71.09, ASTC 0 ETC2 0), built here with g++ and gfxstream's Vulkan headers (no Vulkan pkg-config on this PC, so Meson skips the target here).
- Not done: the AOSP build of `vulkan.apklayer` (the Mac build host did not answer over ssh, nor did the x86 PC), so Endfield itself is not run with it; the clang `-Werror` build of the vendored files is unverified (g++ `-Wall -Wextra` is clean). ETC2 is covered by gfxstream's shaders but not by the test.

ACE's SIGSEGV handler value in these runs is a bogus pointer into libc text (handler = libc +0x7b987 odd, +0x7bbb4, +0x7ab8b: mid-function, different per run), so the handler delivery itself ends in the SIGBUS BUS_ADRALN (odd pc) of the death chain; with libc intact nothing faults. The next libc call that needs errno (a futex wait: `bl __errno@plt`) fetches from the hole: SEGV_MAPERR with pc == si_addr, guest handler bogus (a libc-text pointer, odd or mid-function, different per run) -> SIGBUS BUS_ADRALN at the handler -> self-raise -> EXIT 0.08-0.6 s after the munmap. Limit: the translated side sees only the guest's raw `svc` (libc calls of the guest go to the host's glibc through the proxy and never reach `RunGuestSyscall`), native sees everything, so whole-thread diffs are noisy (native 1.7 M syscalls in 38 s vs 0.93 M translated in 35 s).
- Native reference run on AWS used a private copy of `pgr` with files <= 1 MB only (the 43 GB copy took > 30 min on that disk): the game left after 60-77 s with rc 0 (data missing), ACE started 20 s after the first open. Not a clean control for the data-dependent part.
- **Observed difference (candidate, not yet proven to be the cause):** the translated ACE thread (first opener of `files/ano_tmp/comm.zip`, `tss_ano.dat`) runs, 12 ms after its start and after the `shell_cache/vm/comm.zip` lookups (ENOENT), an emulator-artefact probe list through raw `faccessat` + `newfstatat`, all ENOENT: `/init.vbox86.rc`, `/dev/socket/genyd`, `/data/data/com.tencent.tinput`, `/vendor/lib/libdrm.so.exagear`, `/system/lib/ld-android.so.exagear`, `/system/priv-app/TGPAServer/TGPAServer.apk.exagear`, `init.android_x86.rc`, `ueventd.android_x86.rc`, `/system/framework/x86`. The native run issued none of them in 38 s (greps genyd/exagear/vbox86/tinput/TGPAServer: 0 hits natively, 2 translated; `/dev/virtpipe-sec` is probed by both). So ACE takes an emulator-detection branch only on the translated route: next, find what it reads before (arch/ABI: properties `ro.product.cpu.abi*`, `/proc/cpuinfo` (translated thread 850375 reads it 157 k times), `/proc/sys/kernel/arch`, AT_PLATFORM/auxv, `/system/lib` layout, dirs named x86) and make those the native's.
- Left on the hosts: nothing (tester `~/envT` 46 GB and AWS `~/envN` 5 GB removed, core_pattern restored by the script).

## 2026-11-16: PGR on the tester PC: the true time of death is 28-38 s (the old 106-177 s included systemd-coredump), hello-acediff is clean
- **No build, no translator change.** Own tree on the tester PC (`~/apklayer-build-x/acediff`, meson from main b2cdb476, own instance `acex`, copy instance `trial2` of instance 0, all deleted after); the stack was still the system daemon's with `runtime/current` 0.4.19 (a tree's own meson install does not replace the runtime the shared daemon starts: for a candidate library use a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME as the 2026-11-16 GApps entry says).
- **hello-acediff "dies at start" on the tester PC was a harness effect, not a translation fault.** Its forked children end by SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL/SIGFPE/SIGABRT on purpose (default-action tests of patch 0040); the tester PC's `kernel.core_pattern` is `|systemd-coredump` (the Intel PC's is not), so every such child sat in `do_coredump` (state S, then `anon_pipe_write`) for 80-130 s writing a 330 MB zst core, and the parent's `waitpid` with it; acediff's output is one buffer printed at the end, so no `[acediff]` line ever showed. The "Guest signal 11 ... has no guest handler" line in the log is a child's by-design report. Children now `setrlimit(RLIMIT_CORE, 0)` + `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)` (hello-acediff `NOCORE`): `acediff` on the tester PC (Ryzen 5 5600, translator of the 0.4.19 runtime) finishes in about 60 s and its 363 lines equal real-arm64.txt minus known-diffs.txt (0 differing lines). CPU feature selection (AVX2/VAES/SHA/PCLMUL...) is not involved.
- **True death times of PGR** (new `tools/ace/pgr-timeline.sh` + `.bt`: ACE's files reset before every run, `core_pattern` set to `|/bin/true` for the run and restored, bpftrace of the game process: file opens, kernel fault signals, self-sent signals, process exit; times from the first open by the game's main thread; run on `trial2`): process EXIT at **34.04 s, 33.62 s, 28.39 s** (runs 1-3 of the table) and 35.76 s / 38.0 s in two earlier runs measured from the trace start (about 34 s after the game's start); `apklayer run` rc 135 (SIGBUS) or 139. The 106-177 s of the earlier tables were time-of-process-end including the coredump (`coredumpctl list` on the tester PC has 39799 entries; the PGR processes' cores are "missing" = discarded as too large). So the earlier lifetimes carry no information about drift; the death is a fixed ~34 s after the start, i.e. ~22-33 s after libanogs.so is loaded.
- **What happens at the end (translated):** thread `Thread-68/69` sends itself, in one millisecond: `rt_tgsigqueueinfo(SIGSEGV, si_code 1 SEGV_MAPERR, si_addr 0x7a08...fd0)` (the translator's emulated guest fault), then `rt_tgsigqueueinfo(SIGBUS, si_code 1 BUS_ADRALN, si_addr 0x7a08...42d` odd = a misaligned pc), then `tgkill(self, SIGBUS)`; EXIT 3-5 ms later. Run 3 died differently: 2259 emulated SIGSEGV (code 1, addr 0) in 2 ms on one thread (a loop of a handler returning to the faulting instruction), no tgkill. **Native (AWS pgrtest, 2 runs of 100 s, reset ACE files): zero such faults**, only HotSpot/Unity's usual null and guard-page faults (code 1 addr 0/0x8, code 2 at one stable address). So the deliberate fault chain is ACE's reaction (punishment) after its verdict, not a fault-delivery probe that natively passes: the question stays what ACE concluded at about +4 s to +30 s.
- **Difference found while tracing, in the files ACE writes** (after one run, `ace-after-N`): translated (3 of 3 runs, identical sizes): `ace_shell_di.dat` 22, `ano_tmp/{ace_shell_db.dat 40, ano_app_915c.dat 24, config2.xml.17296724 436, fake_uiui.dat 31, h_rcd.dat 12, kvcache8.dat 137, tersafe.update 4, tp2cfg.dat 612, tss_ano.dat 325}`; native (2 runs): `ano_tmp` stays EMPTY and `ace_shell_di.dat` is gone (ACE writes `.tmp` files of the same names and they do not survive the run; no `tersafe.update`, `tp2cfg.dat` (TenProtect), `tss_ano.dat`, `config2`, `fake_uiui.dat` are ever opened natively). Natively ACE's first opens are `ace_shell_di.dat`, `ano_tmp/ace_cache_db.dat`, `ace_shell_db.dat`, `shell_cache/vm/comm.zip` at 0-0.3 s; translated the first ones are `ano_tmp/tersafe.update` and `tss_ano.dat` (6 s on the trace clock), then `ac_tmp` and `config2.dat.<hash>` (the translated run takes the TerSafe/TP2 branch the native run never enters).
- **`fake_uiui.dat` (+2-4 s, translated only) found mechanically** (new `tools/ace/ace-creat.bt`, uprobe on RunGuestSyscall, openat with O_CREAT: guest x30 + frame chain + maps): the writer of `ano_tmp/fake_uiui.dat.tmp` runs on a worker thread with x30 = libanogs.so +0x338de4 (the return of the obfuscated syscall dispatcher at +0x338d84: `mov w0,#56 (openat)`, `blr x8`), frames +0x3396ec, +0x32280c, +0x2d3824, **+0x1f5238** (the same `blr x1` call thunk the 2026-11-16 free-storm entry names), +0x1f929c. The condition that gates the write was not read (obfuscated; libanogs.so copied to the scratchpad only, `llvm-objdump` of the NDK works on it: `-d --start-address`).

## 2026-11-16: runtime-identity regression after the DelegateLastClassLoader overlay
- Cause: the overlay asks the boot loader first (java.lang.BootClassLoader, which answers from the sandbox), and that also finds the app's own classes (defined by a dex loader), so a `DelegateLastClassLoader` over the app's own base.apk returned the app's class instead of defining its own: `Android-visible APK path was not mapped and loaded by its DelegateLastClassLoader`. Path mapping (ShadowHostBaseDexClassLoader.hostPath) was never the problem.
- Fix (overlay): a boot-loader hit whose class is defined by a BaseDexClassLoader (an app class) is not a boot-path class and is skipped, as on a device; platform classes and the NPE fix are unchanged.
- Test: `DynamicDexChecks` ran Probe through a DelegateLastClassLoader expecting the parent APK's `payload.ParentContext` (a delegate-first result, wrong for this loader): DelegateLast now only has to define Probe and ParentContext itself; added the Dynamite-shaped checks (platform class from the boot path, missing class is ClassNotFoundException, no NPE).
- Verified on the UTM VM in an own tree (`APKLY_VM_ROOT=~/apklayer-dlcl`, slots dl1-4; the default `~/apklayer` is shared, and runs against it were corrupted by other pushes): runtime-identity, identity-matrix, providers, activities 3/3 (activities failed once at exit-deadline's spare case on a fresh state dir, `run.*` file with a package name), runtime-identity 3 more times alone. files-gapps-etc passed 3/3 in the shared tree, but cannot start in a new tree path (sandbox: AppArmor denies user-namespace capabilities, `sudo tools/host-setup/sandbox.sh` per path).
- Not run: Play services itself (no Google login); the NPE regression is covered by the loadClass checks. Known limit: converter metadata (DenyInstrument parentFirst) still treats the parent's class as the one used for a duplicate class in a delegate-last dex.
- PLAN: none open from this.
